topic: Reactions of Alkenes and Markovnikov's Rule
title: Markovnikov's Rule Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
An open hand catches a ball, an empty seat takes a new passenger and a free hook holds a new coat. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 9, Hydrocarbons) Aarav finds that almost every reaction of alkenes is one move: open the pi bond and add two new pieces.

On the molecule bench, hydrogen, bromine and hydrogen halides add across C=C (HI > HBr > HCl). Curved arrows show HBr adding to propene through a carbocation, the secondary carbocation wins, and we get 2-bromopropane: Markovnikov's rule. Then the peroxide effect (Kharash effect) link by link with free radicals, why HCl and HI do not show it, a worked ozonolysis example (ethanal + methanal gives propene), additions of sulphuric acid and water, Baeyer's reagent, acidic permanganate and polymerisation, the exam trap, an original JEE pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 93 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Open the pi bond, add two pieces
0:27 Why alkenes add: H2, Br2 test, HX order
1:04 HBr + propene: the carbocation mechanism
1:50 Markovnikov's rule
2:05 Pause and think: propene + HCl
2:15 Peroxide effect, link by link
3:10 Worked example: ozonolysis
3:52 More additions, Baeyer's reagent, polymerisation
4:26 Exam trap: where does H go?
4:50 Practice question (JEE pattern)
5:29 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Alkynes. Why can ethyne give away a hydrogen like an acid, when ethene cannot?
